tools.name: best_card_for_purchase
tools.description: Which credit card earns the most rewards for a purchase, and why. With no cards given and no saved wallet, it ranks every card earnrate knows (in `allCards`): a complete answer for anyone. With cards named in the conversation (`cards`) or a saved wallet, it picks the best of the user's own: `decision.cardId` is the pick and `decision.checkoutLabel` is how the card appears at checkout, with every usable card ranked with reasons, cards the merchant won't take, assumptions, warnings, and when a different point valuation would change the pick. For a business earnrate may not know, like a local restaurant, pass `category` when you can tell what kind of business it is. When the user is paying outside the U.S. or in another currency, pass `country`: abroad, each card is ranked after its foreign transaction fee. Pass `payment` only when the user says how they're paying, like Apple Pay or PayPal checkout. A statement credit (a card's `credit`, like Amex Platinum's lululemon credit) counts toward the pick only once it's enrolled in the wallet and has dollars left this period, and only when the amount is given; say its dollars apart from the % back. With no cards, `allCards.credits` lists cards with a credit at the store; present those first. Never needs or returns card numbers.

Optional; omit it when unknown, and never assume Apple Pay. Some rates need one (Apple Card's 2% with Apple Pay, PayPal Cashback's 3% through PayPal checkout), and the answer's assumptions say when paying another way would change the pick.

tools.description: Ranks cards the user doesn't have by what they'd be worth over the first two years: what each adds to the user's cards (or, with none, earns) on their spending, plus the public welcome (sign-up) bonus in year one if its minimum spend fits in the window, less each year's annual fee. Each offer also shows the bonus alone (first-year value), year one and year two, and how many weeks of spending the minimum takes. Offers the issuer rules out because of a card in the user's wallet are marked likely not eligible and listed last; issuers the user can't get cards from (skippedIssuers, or saved with set_memberships) are left out. Use it when the user asks which card to get next or which has the best sign-up bonus. Spending is optional (typical amounts otherwise). It covers only the cards earnrate knows, offers vary by person, and each offer's note gives the issuer's eligibility rules; pass those caveats on. Never suggest applying through a link.

tools.name: search_cards
tools.description: Finds credit cards in earnrate's catalog by name or issuer, e.g. "sapphire", "amex gold" or "bofa". Returns each card's id (for add_card), network, annual fee (and any first-year waiver), foreign transaction fee, whether it's already in the wallet, what it needs set up (category picks and their options, memberships, activations), its yearly spend bonuses, first-year rates, statement credits and yearly free nights (valued at their point cap, "up to"), each with the id update_card takes. When it finds 3 cards or fewer, also each card's earning rates (with a note on how they're counted where they'd read oddly), its published welcome offer, its recent changes and, for a card with an annual fee, whether the fee is worth it: the monthly spending in its bonus categories at which it nets more than the best no-fee card, and the same with all its statement credits and free nights used, on typical U.S. spending at the saved point values (earnrate's defaults without them, and again at transfer value for Amex and Chase points). Call it for "is the <card> worth it?" or "is its annual fee worth it?" and quote that line. Leave the query out to list every card. US cards only.

query.description: Card name or issuer, as the user said it.

tools.name: list_wallet
tools.description: Starts with a to-do list for the user's cards right now (bonuses to activate and their deadlines, categories to pick or confirm, caps nearly used up, welcome bonuses to finish and the weekly pace, yearly spend bonuses at least 75% of the way, statement credits to enroll in or use before they reset, whether the user uses a card's credits and yearly free night, and a fee card's renewal check in the month before its anniversary: whether it still pays for itself at typical spending; then, for 60 days, changes an issuer made to the user's cards, with the old and new terms and the issuer's page, and one line per card for earnrate's corrections to its own data about it, which are earnrate's mistakes and not the issuer's); use it when the user asks what to do with their cards this quarter or what they're forgetting. Then lists the user's cards: checkout label, network, rewards currency and its value, spending caps with how much is left this period, chosen bonus categories (and whether they're current), welcome-bonus progress, progress toward yearly spend bonuses, statement credits (enrolled or not, and what's left this period), yearly free nights (used or not, and what one is worth to the user if they said), which stores a store card works at, when each card's data was last verified, the point values the user saved, and (for the hosted wallet) when it was started. It uses the wallet file on this computer, not the hosted earnrate connector's wallet.

tools.name: record_purchase
tools.description: Records a purchase the user has already made, so spending caps, welcome-bonus progress, yearly spend bonuses and statement credits used stay accurate for future recommendations. It updates the user's saved wallet. Only call it after the purchase has happened, and only once per purchase: calling it twice counts the spend twice. Purchases with no cap, no open welcome bonus, no spend bonus and no enrolled statement credit are acknowledged and nothing is written. For a merchant earnrate doesn't recognize it asks for category first, so caps aren't missed. It uses the wallet file on this computer, not the hosted earnrate connector's wallet.

by.description: The deadline, YYYY-MM-DD, only if the user's offer differs from the published one.

tools.name: update_card
tools.description: Changes settings on a card already in the wallet: its category picks for this period, checkout label, anniversary, opening date (optional; for first-year rates), activated categories, cap spending so far (capSpent), spending this year toward its spend bonuses (milestoneSpent), statement credits enrolled in and free nights used (enrolled), credits used this period (creditUsed), credits or free nights not used at all (skippedCredits), what a free night is worth to the user (nightValues, only if they say), or a welcome bonus to track. Picks replace the saved ones in each choice group you set (other groups are kept) for the current period. Use it when the user picks new categories, such as each quarter on U.S. Bank Cash+. It uses the wallet file on this computer, not the hosted earnrate connector's wallet.

cardId.description: The card id from search_cards, e.g. chase-sapphire-preferred.

checkoutLabel.description: How the card appears at checkout or in a browser wallet, e.g. "Amex Gold". Optional; null goes back to the card's own name.

picks.description: For cards where the cardholder picks bonus categories: choice id → option ids, from search_cards, e.g. {"five-percent": ["tv-internet-streaming", "fast-food"]}. Saved for the current period. Ask the user; don't guess.

anniversary.description: The account's anniversary as MM-DD: for cards whose cap resets on it, and for a fee card's renewal check (whether it still pays for itself before the fee comes due). Optional; the opening date stands in. Ask; don't guess.

opened.description: Optional: the day the account opened, YYYY-MM-DD. Only for cards with a first-year rate (search_cards lists it), which applies only while a purchase falls in the window; without a date the card is ranked at its standard rates. Ask the user; never guess or assume a card is new. null removes it.

activated.description: Rule ids the user has activated with the issuer, such as rotating categories. Replaces the current list.

capSpent.description: Dollars already spent this period on a capped bonus, for a card the user starts tracking partway through: cap key (as list_wallet shows it) → dollars, e.g. {"five-percent-quarterly": 400}. Ask; recorded purchases add to it from then on.

milestoneSpent.description: Dollars already spent on the card this year, for its spend bonuses (bonuses after a yearly spending total, as search_cards lists them): milestone id → dollars, e.g. {"spend-15k": 9000}. Every purchase on the card counts, so give each milestone the same total. Ask; recorded purchases add to it from then on.

enrolled.description: Statement credit ids the user has enrolled in with the issuer, or, for a credit that needs no enrolling, says they use, and free night ids they say they use (search_cards and list_wallet list each card's credits and free nights, e.g. "lululemon" on Amex Platinum, "anniversary-night" on IHG Premier). A credit that needs enrolling counts in answers only once it's here, and any credit or free night counts against the annual fee only once it's here (or, for a credit, has been used). Replaces the current list. Ask; never assume.

creditUsed.description: Dollars of a statement credit already received this period: credit id → dollars, e.g. {"lululemon": 40}. Ask; recorded purchases add to it from then on.

skippedCredits.description: Statement credit and free night ids the user doesn't use, e.g. ["dunkin"] on Amex Gold. They're left out of picks, the to-do list and the annual-fee math; every other credit or free night on the card counts against its fee once it's in enrolled (or, for a credit that needs no enrolling, has been used). Replaces the current list; [] counts them all again.

nightValues.description: What a yearly free night is worth to the user, in dollars, only if they say: free night id → dollars, e.g. {"anniversary-night": 300}. The night then counts at that instead of its point cap, and a night with no point cap counts only this way. Setting one marks the night used, even when enrolled in the same call leaves it out (only skippedCredits naming it says otherwise). null clears it; other nights keep theirs.

bonus.description: A welcome bonus the user is working toward, so purchases recorded on this card count toward it and answers can favor it. Ask when they opened the account; spending needed and the deadline default to the card's published offer. null stops tracking it.

opened.description: The day the account opened, YYYY-MM-DD.

spent.description: Dollars already spent toward the bonus. Default 0.

spend.description: Dollars of spending the bonus needs, only if the user's offer differs from the published one.

by.description: The deadline, YYYY-MM-DD, only if the user's offer differs from the published one.

tools.name: remove_card
tools.description: Removes a card from the wallet, with its tracked cap usage, bonus progress and yearly spending. Memberships and point values stay, even when the last card goes. Only when the user says they no longer have it or don't want it considered. It uses the wallet file on this computer, not the hosted earnrate connector's wallet.

cardId.description: The card id from search_cards, e.g. chase-sapphire-preferred.

tools.name: set_memberships
tools.description: Sets the memberships that unlock some cards' rates, such as amazon-prime for Prime Visa's 5% or a Bank of America Preferred Rewards tier, and costco for a Costco membership (so spending answers don't count its cost against Costco Anywhere). Replaces the whole list, so include the ones to keep. It saves them even with no cards saved, and every answer then uses them. With skippedIssuers, it also saves the issuers the user can't or won't get a new card from (Chase over its 5/24 rule), which next-card answers leave out; either can be given alone. It uses the wallet file on this computer, not the hosted earnrate connector's wallet.

memberships.description: Every membership the user has. Known: amazon-prime, bank-of-america-account, bank-of-america-small-business-account, bofa-rewards-member, bofa-rewards-preferred-honors, bofa-rewards-preferred-plus, bofa-rewards-premier, caltech-efcu, costco, navy-federal, nordy-club-ambassador, penfed-honors-advantage, rei-co-op, sams-club, sams-club-plus, usbank-smartly-100, usbank-smartly-25, usbank-smartly-50, verizon-account.

skippedIssuers.description: Issuers the user says they can't or won't get a new card from (for example Chase, over its 5/24 rule): left out of compare_welcome_offers and of the cards that would add the most. Replaces the saved list; [] clears it. Ask; never assume.

tools.name: set_point_values
tools.description: Saves what the user's points are worth to them, in cents per point, in their saved wallet; every answer then compares cards at those values unless a valuation profile is asked for. No saved cards are needed. Use it when the user says what their points are worth ("I value Chase points at 1.5¢") or that they transfer points to airlines and hotels (profile points-heavy). Values change only the currencies given; null goes back to earnrate's default. Currencies by id: cash (Cash back), MR (Amex Membership Rewards), UR (Chase Ultimate Rewards), sofi-rewards (SoFi Member Rewards), bofa-travel-rewards (Bank of America Travel Rewards points), bofa-premium-rewards (Bank of America Premium Rewards points), usbank-altitude (U.S. Bank Altitude points), navy-federal-rewards (Navy Federal Rewards points), rei-rewards (REI Co-op Mastercard rewards), best-buy-rewards (My Best Buy rewards), C1 (Capital One miles), TYP (Citi ThankYou points), WFR (Wells Fargo Rewards), BILT (Bilt points), united-miles (United MileagePlus miles), aadvantage-miles (American Airlines AAdvantage miles), southwest-rapid-rewards (Southwest Rapid Rewards points), aeroplan (Aeroplan points), atmos-points (Atmos Rewards points), trueblue-points (JetBlue TrueBlue points), ihg-points (IHG One Rewards points), delta-skymiles (Delta SkyMiles), hilton-honors (Hilton Honors points), marriott-bonvoy (Marriott Bonvoy points), kohls-rewards (Kohl's Rewards), nordy-club (Nordy Club points). It uses the wallet file on this computer, not the hosted earnrate connector's wallet.

values.description: Cents per point by currency id, e.g. {"UR": 1.5, "MR": 1.6}. null goes back to the default.

profile.description: A preset: flat (MR and UR at 1¢) or points-heavy (MR and UR at 1.7¢). Values given too win over it.

instructions:
earnrate answers which credit card earns the most for a purchase, from each issuer's own terms. Anyone can use it without entering anything: with no cards given, best_card_for_purchase, best_cards_for, cheat_sheet, simulate_spending and compare_welcome_offers answer from every card earnrate knows, and that's a complete answer. Never require the user's cards, and don't ask what they spend unless the answer depends on it; simulate_spending assumes typical amounts when none are given and says so.

Personalizing is optional. If the user names their cards, pass them as `cards` (ids from search_cards) for that answer; nothing is saved. After answering, offer once to save those cards so earnrate remembers them, and save them with add_card only if the user says yes. Only if they want earnrate to remember their cards, track spending caps or welcome bonuses, or record purchases, save a wallet with add_card and the other wallet tools. When a card needs category picks, memberships like Amazon Prime, or activations, ask the user rather than guessing. When the user asks what to do with their cards (this quarter, or what they're forgetting), call list_wallet: it starts with a to-do list.

The wallet lists cards by product id, never card numbers; never ask for card numbers, expiry dates or security codes.

This server's saved wallet is a file on the user's computer. The earnrate extension on the user's computer and the hosted earnrate connector keep separate wallets with the same tools. If both are connected, say which wallet an answer comes from, and ask the user which one to use before saving or recording anything.
